source.primary_manuscript: Codex Vaticanus (B/03; Vatican Library Gr. 1209, 4th c. CE ~325-350)
source.primary_manuscript_contains: Essentially complete New Testament (with some Hebrews + Pauline epistles lacunae); complete Matthew
source.secondary_manuscript: Codex Sinaiticus (א/01; British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments, 4th c. CE ~330-360)
source.early_papyri_cross_collation: P45 (Chester Beatty I; 3rd c. CE ~250) preserves portions of Matthew 25 — specifically vv.41-26:39 in the surviving leaves — providing the earliest substantial papyrus witness to the Sheep-and-Goats final-judgment pericope. P45 readings substantially agree with Vaticanus + Sinaiticus at the level of textual baseline; minor orthographic variants are noted per verse where relevant.
source.reference_critical_apparatus: NA28 (Nestle-Aland 28th, 2012); UBS5 (United Bible Societies 5th, 2014); SBLGNT (SBL 2010); THGNT (Tyndale House 2017)
source.transliteration_convention: Scholarly Koine Greek transliteration (SBL convention): polytonic-stripped lowercase Latin with diacritics for breathings (h- for rough; nothing for smooth) and Greek-specific letters (ē for eta, ō for omega, ph for phi, ch for chi, ps for psi, th for theta, rh for rho with rough breathing); ai/ei/oi/au/eu/ou diphthongs preserved; accent marks generally omitted in scholarly translit
source.verificationStatus: best-effort reconstruction; verification pending against Vaticanus + Sinaiticus + P45 original codicology + the NA28/UBS5/SBLGNT critical apparatus
source.fetchedFrom: SBLGNT public-domain edition (Holmes 2010) + NA28 reference + P45 readings per Kenyon, F. G., *The Chester Beatty Biblical Papyri* (London 1933-1937) and Comfort & Barrett *Text of the Earliest NT Greek MSS* (2001).
source.citation: Aland, Aland, Karavidopoulos, Martini, Metzger, eds., *Novum Testamentum Graece*, 28th ed. (Nestle-Aland, Stuttgart 2012). UBS5 = Aland et al., *The Greek New Testament*, 5th ed. (United Bible Societies 2014). Holmes, M. W., ed., *The Greek New Testament: SBL Edition* (SBL 2010; public-domain). Jongkind, D., ed., *The Greek New Testament*, Tyndale House (Crossway 2017). Codex Vaticanus: Vatican Library Gr. 1209 (4th c. CE). Codex Sinaiticus: British Library Add. 43725 + Sinai + Leipzig + St. Petersburg fragments (4th c. CE). P45 = Chester Beatty I (3rd c. CE). Davies-Allison ICC 1988-1997 (vol 3); Luz Hermeneia 2001-2005 (vol 3); France NICNT 2007; Hagner WBC 1995; Nolland NIGTC 2005; Jeremias, J., *The Parables of Jesus* (Scribner's 1972); Snodgrass, K., *Stories with Intent* (Eerdmans 2008); Gray, S. W., *The Least of My Brothers: Matthew 25:31-46 — A History of Interpretation* (Scholars Press 1989); Wilkins, M. J., *Discipleship in the Ancient World and Matthew's Gospel* (Baker 1995); Levine-Brettler JANT 2017.
source.paleography_note: The Koine Greek text is preserved in polytonic form as transmitted via SBLGNT. The early Greek manuscripts use scriptio continua. Nomina sacra (ΙΣ, ΧΣ, ΚΣ, ΘΣ, ΥΣ, ΠΗΡ) appear abbreviated in the uncials. The Sheep-and-Goats pericope (vv.31-46) is preserved with minimal text-critical disturbance; the P45 cross-collation for vv.41-46 confirms the consensus reading.

verses.text: Τότε ὁμοιωθήσεται ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν δέκα παρθένοις, αἵτινες λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας ἑαυτῶν ἐξῆλθον εἰς ὑπάντησιν τοῦ νυμφίου.
verses.translit: Tote homoiōthēsetai hē basileia tōn ouranōn deka parthenois, haitines labousai tas lampadas heautōn exēlthon eis hypantēsin tou nymphiou.
verses.notes: **PARABLE OF THE TEN VIRGINS — OPENING (vv.1-13)**. Matthew-only material (no synoptic parallel). Part of Matthew's Discourse 5 (the Olivet / eschatological discourse — chs. 24-25). *homoiōthēsetai* (will be likened) — future passive, Matthean parable-formula. *parthenoi* = virgins / young unmarried women, the standard bridal-attendants role at 1st-c. Jewish weddings. *lampades* — disputed: 'lamps' (small oil-lamps) or 'torches' (rags soaked in oil on a stick; Jeremias 1972 174-175 argues for torches based on archaeological evidence and the need for added oil at v.4). *eis hypantēsin tou nymphiou* — the formal procession-out-to-meet-the-bridegroom. The bridegroom's late arrival is the structural pivot. Davies-Allison ICC 3.391-400; Luz Hermeneia 3.227-238; Snodgrass 2008 505-528. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: the bridegroom-delay topos is canon-engaged by Raël (and broader ancient-astronaut readings) as 'awaiting the Elohim's return' — preserve text, document for Editor.

verses.text: πέντε δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν ἦσαν μωραὶ καὶ πέντε φρόνιμοι.
verses.translit: pente de ex autōn ēsan mōrai kai pente phronimoi.
verses.notes: *mōrai* (foolish) vs *phronimoi* (prudent / sensible) — Matthean wisdom-vocabulary inherited from sapiential tradition (cf. Prov 1-9 LXX *phronēsis*). The 5-vs-5 split is the parable's structural dualism; Matthean parables frequently sort hearers into binary categories (wheat/tares, sheep/goats, wise/foolish builders).

verses.text: αἱ γὰρ μωραὶ λαβοῦσαι τὰς λαμπάδας αὐτῶν οὐκ ἔλαβον μεθ' ἑαυτῶν ἔλαιον·
verses.translit: hai gar mōrai labousai tas lampadas autōn ouk elabon meth' heautōn elaion·
verses.notes: The oil-deficit — foundational to the parable's allegory. Patristic allegorical readings construed the oil variously as good works (Chrysostom), the Holy Spirit (Augustine), or perseverance (Origen). Modern parable-scholarship (Jeremias 1972; Snodgrass 2008) tends to read the oil as a particular figure within the parable's eschatological-readiness structure rather than allegorize it specifically.

verses.text: αἱ δὲ φρόνιμοι ἔλαβον ἔλαιον ἐν τοῖς ἀγγείοις μετὰ τῶν λαμπάδων ἑαυτῶν.
verses.translit: hai de phronimoi elabon elaion en tois angeiois meta tōn lampadōn heautōn.
verses.notes: *angeia* (vessels / flasks) — additional oil-containers. Jeremias 1972 174-175 takes this as supporting the torch-reading (torches were dipped in additional oil for refueling during long processions).

verses.text: χρονίζοντος δὲ τοῦ νυμφίου ἐνύσταξαν πᾶσαι καὶ ἐκάθευδον.
verses.translit: chronizontos de tou nymphiou enystaxan pasai kai ekatheudon.
verses.notes: **THE BRIDEGROOM-DELAY MOTIF**. *chronizontos* (delaying) — the same root as the Matthean *chronizei mou ho kyrios* (my master is delayed) at Mt 24:48 (the wicked-servant pericope, immediately preceding). The delay-of-the-Parousia is a deliberate Matthean redactional theme addressing the late-1st-c. crisis of the unfulfilled imminent expectation. Note: BOTH wise and foolish virgins fall asleep — sleep is not the failure; preparation-for-delay is the metric. Davies-Allison ICC 3.396-397.

verses.text: μέσης δὲ νυκτὸς κραυγὴ γέγονεν· Ἰδοὺ ὁ νυμφίος, ἐξέρχεσθε εἰς ἀπάντησιν.
verses.translit: mesēs de nyktos kraugē gegonen· Idou ho nymphios, exerchesthe eis apantēsin.
verses.notes: *mesēs nyktos* (at midnight) — the thief-in-the-night / unexpected-hour eschatological topos (cf. Mt 24:43; 1 Thess 5:2). *kraugē* (a cry / shout) — the herald-cry of the Parousia (cf. 1 Thess 4:16 *en kraugē*). Variant: some witnesses add *tou nymphiou* (of the bridegroom) after *apantēsin*; SBLGNT/NA28 omit.

verses.text: τότε ἠγέρθησαν πᾶσαι αἱ παρθένοι ἐκεῖναι καὶ ἐκόσμησαν τὰς λαμπάδας ἑαυτῶν.
verses.translit: tote ēgerthēsan pasai hai parthenoi ekeinai kai ekosmēsan tas lampadas heautōn.
verses.notes: *ekosmēsan* (trimmed / put in order) — preparing the lamps/torches for the procession. *ēgerthēsan* (rose / were raised) — same verb-root as the resurrection (*egeirō*); possibly deliberate eschatological echo (the cry-of-awakening at the end-of-the-age).

verses.text: αἱ δὲ μωραὶ ταῖς φρονίμοις εἶπαν· Δότε ἡμῖν ἐκ τοῦ ἐλαίου ὑμῶν, ὅτι αἱ λαμπάδες ἡμῶν σβέννυνται.
verses.translit: hai de mōrai tais phronimois eipan· Dote hēmin ek tou elaiou hymōn, hoti hai lampades hēmōn sbennyntai.
verses.notes: *sbennyntai* (are going out) — present tense, the lamps are in process of failing. The crisis: oil cannot be shared across persons in the parable's economy — the wise-vs-foolish line is irreducible.

verses.text: ἀπεκρίθησαν δὲ αἱ φρόνιμοι λέγουσαι· Μήποτε οὐ μὴ ἀρκέσῃ ἡμῖν καὶ ὑμῖν· πορεύεσθε μᾶλλον πρὸς τοὺς πωλοῦντας καὶ ἀγοράσατε ἑαυταῖς.
verses.translit: apekrithēsan de hai phronimoi legousai· Mēpote ou mē arkesē hēmin kai hymin· poreuesthe mallon pros tous pōlountas kai agorasate heautais.
verses.notes: The wise refuse — the parable's hard edge. *mēpote* (lest somehow) introduces a polite-formal hesitation; the refusal is not selfishness but parable-logic (the eschatological readiness cannot be transferred between persons). The midnight-merchant-shopping detail is improbable as historical detail and signals the parable's allegorical-not-realistic mode.

verses.text: ἀπερχομένων δὲ αὐτῶν ἀγοράσαι ἦλθεν ὁ νυμφίος, καὶ αἱ ἕτοιμοι εἰσῆλθον μετ' αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς γάμους, καὶ ἐκλείσθη ἡ θύρα.
verses.translit: aperchomenōn de autōn agorasai ēlthen ho nymphios, kai hai hetoimoi eisēlthon met' autou eis tous gamous, kai ekleisthē hē thyra.
verses.notes: *hai hetoimoi* (the ready ones) — the parable's central thematic word. *gamous* = wedding-feast / wedding-banquet (plural in Greek). *ekleisthē hē thyra* (the door was shut) — the closure-of-the-door image: the irreversible eschatological boundary (cf. Luke 13:25; Mt 7:23 *ouk oida hymas*). Patristic and modern interpreters alike read this as the door-of-the-final-judgment.

verses.text: ὕστερον δὲ ἔρχονται καὶ αἱ λοιπαὶ παρθένοι λέγουσαι· Κύριε κύριε, ἄνοιξον ἡμῖν.
verses.translit: hysteron de erchontai kai hai loipai parthenoi legousai· Kyrie kyrie, anoixon hēmin.
verses.notes: *Kyrie kyrie* — the doubled vocative — echoes Mt 7:21-23 (*ou pas ho legōn moi Kyrie kyrie eiseleusetai*) and Luke 6:46. The Matthean intra-corpus parallel signals the same judgment-of-the-falsely-confident motif.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐκ οἶδα ὑμᾶς.
verses.translit: ho de apokritheis eipen· Amēn legō hymin, ouk oida hymas.
verses.notes: *ouk oida hymas* (I do not know you) — verbatim parallel to Mt 7:23 *oudepote egnōn hymas* ('I never knew you'). The pronouncement-of-rejection. Davies-Allison ICC 3.400.

verses.text: γρηγορεῖτε οὖν, ὅτι οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν ἡμέραν οὐδὲ τὴν ὥραν.
verses.translit: grēgoreite oun, hoti ouk oidate tēn hēmeran oude tēn hōran.
verses.notes: **THE WATCHFULNESS-EXHORTATION**. *grēgoreite* (keep watch / stay awake) — Matthean signature watchfulness-verb (cf. 24:42; 26:38, 40, 41). Note the parable-logic tension: in v.5 ALL the virgins slept; the exhortation *grēgoreite* therefore cannot mean literal sleeplessness but rather eschatological preparedness. Variant: many Byzantine witnesses add *en hē ho huios tou anthrōpou erchetai* (in which the Son of Man comes) — a harmonizing assimilation from Mt 24:44; SBLGNT/NA28 omit. Davies-Allison ICC 3.400-401.

verses.text: Ὥσπερ γὰρ ἄνθρωπος ἀποδημῶν ἐκάλεσεν τοὺς ἰδίους δούλους καὶ παρέδωκεν αὐτοῖς τὰ ὑπάρχοντα αὐτοῦ,
verses.translit: Hōsper gar anthrōpos apodēmōn ekalesen tous idious doulous kai paredōken autois ta hyparchonta autou,
verses.notes: **PARABLE OF THE TALENTS — OPENING (vv.14-30)**. Synoptic parallel: Luke 19:11-27 (the parable of the minas — differs significantly in detail and likely a separate parabolic tradition rather than a direct synoptic parallel). *apodēmōn* (going on a journey / departing abroad) — the absentee-master topos. *paredōken* (handed over) — same verb as Mt 17:22 etc. (passion-prediction *paradidosthai*). Davies-Allison ICC 3.402-411; Luz Hermeneia 3.249-272; Snodgrass 2008 522-549.

verses.text: καὶ ᾧ μὲν ἔδωκεν πέντε τάλαντα ᾧ δὲ δύο ᾧ δὲ ἕν, ἑκάστῳ κατὰ τὴν ἰδίαν δύναμιν, καὶ ἀπεδήμησεν. εὐθέως
verses.translit: kai hō men edōken pente talanta hō de dyo hō de hen, hekastō kata tēn idian dynamin, kai apedēmēsen. eutheōs
verses.notes: *talanton* — a unit of silver = approximately 6,000 denarii = ~20 years of a laborer's wages — enormous sums. The 5/2/1 distribution *kata tēn idian dynamin* (according to each one's ability) is a key interpretive datum: differential entrustment matches capacity, so the judgment is on use-of-what-was-given, not on absolute-amount. Note: SBLGNT/NA28 attach *eutheōs* (immediately) to the end of v.15 going with v.16; THGNT and Byzantine tradition attach it to the start of v.16. Punctuation only.

verses.text: πορευθεὶς ὁ τὰ πέντε τάλαντα λαβὼν ἠργάσατο ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα πέντε·
verses.translit: poreutheis ho ta pente talanta labōn ērgasato en autois kai ekerdēsen alla pente·
verses.notes: The first servant's entrepreneurial action — *ērgasato* (worked / traded) + *ekerdēsen* (gained). 100% return.

verses.text: ὡσαύτως ὁ τὰ δύο ἐκέρδησεν ἄλλα δύο·
verses.translit: hōsautōs ho ta dyo ekerdēsen alla dyo·
verses.notes: The second servant's parallel action — 100% return.

verses.text: ὁ δὲ τὸ ἓν λαβὼν ἀπελθὼν ὤρυξεν γῆν καὶ ἔκρυψεν τὸ ἀργύριον τοῦ κυρίου αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: ho de to hen labōn apelthōn ōryxen gēn kai ekrypsen to argyrion tou kyriou autou.
verses.notes: *ōryxen gēn kai ekrypsen* (dug ground and hid). Burying as a means of safe-keeping was a 1st-c. recognized practice (cf. m. Bava Metzia 3:10-11 — rabbinic discussion of liability for buried-vs-otherwise-stored deposits; burial was held to be the most prudent storage method, exonerating the bailee). The third servant's action is thus prudentially conservative — a key irony of the parable: the prudent action is judged unfaithful. Davies-Allison ICC 3.406.

verses.text: μετὰ δὲ πολὺν χρόνον ἔρχεται ὁ κύριος τῶν δούλων ἐκείνων καὶ συναίρει λόγον μετ' αὐτῶν
verses.translit: meta de polyn chronon erchetai ho kyrios tōn doulōn ekeinōn kai synairei logon met' autōn
verses.notes: *meta de polyn chronon* (after a long time) — the delayed-return motif (cf. v.5 *chronizontos*). *synairei logon* (settles accounts) — financial-accounting metaphor for the eschatological reckoning.

verses.text: καὶ προσελθὼν ὁ τὰ πέντε τάλαντα λαβὼν προσήνεγκεν ἄλλα πέντε τάλαντα λέγων· Κύριε, πέντε τάλαντά μοι παρέδωκας· ἴδε ἄλλα πέντε τάλαντα ἐκέρδησα.
verses.translit: kai proselthōn ho ta pente talanta labōn prosēnegken alla pente talanta legōn· Kyrie, pente talanta moi paredōkas· ide alla pente talanta ekerdēsa.
verses.notes: The first servant's report — formal accounting-speech. Note the address *Kyrie* (lord/master).

verses.text: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ· Εὖ, δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ, ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἦς πιστός, ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω· εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου σου.
verses.translit: ephē autō ho kyrios autou· Eu, doule agathe kai piste, epi oliga ēs pistos, epi pollōn se katastēsō· eiselthe eis tēn charan tou kyriou sou.
verses.notes: **THE COMMENDATION FORMULA** — verbatim repeated at v.23 for the second servant. *eu, doule agathe kai piste* (well done, good and faithful servant). *eiselthe eis tēn charan* (enter into the joy) — eschatological-banquet idiom (cf. Mt 8:11; 22:1-14). The *charan* (joy) figure is the eschatological-reward image. Davies-Allison ICC 3.407.

verses.text: προσελθὼν δὲ καὶ ὁ τὰ δύο τάλαντα εἶπεν· Κύριε, δύο τάλαντά μοι παρέδωκας· ἴδε ἄλλα δύο τάλαντα ἐκέρδησα.
verses.translit: proselthōn de kai ho ta dyo talanta eipen· Kyrie, dyo talanta moi paredōkas· ide alla dyo talanta ekerdēsa.
verses.notes: Parallel report from the second servant — same accounting-speech form.

verses.text: ἔφη αὐτῷ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ· Εὖ, δοῦλε ἀγαθὲ καὶ πιστέ, ἐπὶ ὀλίγα ἦς πιστός, ἐπὶ πολλῶν σε καταστήσω· εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν χαρὰν τοῦ κυρίου σου.
verses.translit: ephē autō ho kyrios autou· Eu, doule agathe kai piste, epi oliga ēs pistos, epi pollōn se katastēsō· eiselthe eis tēn charan tou kyriou sou.
verses.notes: Verbatim repeat of v.21's commendation — equal reward for the differential entrustment. The 5-talent and 2-talent servants receive identical praise; faithfulness-with-what-was-given is the metric, not absolute output.

verses.text: προσελθὼν δὲ καὶ ὁ τὸ ἓν τάλαντον εἰληφὼς εἶπεν· Κύριε, ἔγνων σε ὅτι σκληρὸς εἶ ἄνθρωπος, θερίζων ὅπου οὐκ ἔσπειρας καὶ συνάγων ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισας·
verses.translit: proselthōn de kai ho to hen talanton eilēphōs eipen· Kyrie, egnōn se hoti sklēros ei anthrōpos, therizōn hopou ouk espeiras kai synagōn hothen ou dieskorpisas·
verses.notes: The third servant's accusation — characterizing the master as *sklēros* (hard / harsh) — *therizōn hopou ouk espeiras* (reaping where you did not sow). The accusation echoes ANE/Greco-Roman absentee-landowner topoi; the parable does not endorse the characterization, but the master will answer on its own terms (v.26). Davies-Allison ICC 3.408-409.

verses.text: καὶ φοβηθεὶς ἀπελθὼν ἔκρυψα τὸ τάλαντόν σου ἐν τῇ γῇ· ἴδε ἔχεις τὸ σόν.
verses.translit: kai phobētheis apelthōn ekrypsa to talanton sou en tē gē· ide echeis to son.
verses.notes: *phobētheis* (being afraid) — fear as the third servant's stated motivation. *echeis to son* (you have what is yours) — the legal-restitution formula: the deposit is returned intact.

verses.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ κύριος αὐτοῦ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Πονηρὲ δοῦλε καὶ ὀκνηρέ, ᾔδεις ὅτι θερίζω ὅπου οὐκ ἔσπειρα καὶ συνάγω ὅθεν οὐ διεσκόρπισα;
verses.translit: apokritheis de ho kyrios autou eipen autō· Ponēre doule kai oknēre, ēdeis hoti therizō hopou ouk espeira kai synagō hothen ou dieskorpisa;
verses.notes: *ponēre doule kai oknēre* (wicked and slothful servant) — the master's response, taking up the servant's characterization on its own terms (the *ēdeis* introduces a quasi-rhetorical concessive). *oknēros* (slothful / hesitant) — Matthew-only NT word; LXX Prov 6:6, 9; 26:14 — wisdom-tradition vocabulary.

verses.text: ἔδει σε οὖν βαλεῖν τὰ ἀργύριά μου τοῖς τραπεζίταις, καὶ ἐλθὼν ἐγὼ ἐκομισάμην ἂν τὸ ἐμὸν σὺν τόκῳ.
verses.translit: edei se oun balein ta argyria mou tois trapezitais, kai elthōn egō ekomisamēn an to emon syn tokō.
verses.notes: *trapezitai* (bankers / money-changers) — the 1st-c. equivalent of interest-bearing-deposit institutions. *syn tokō* (with interest) — note: this is in tension with Torah-prohibitions on interest from a fellow-Israelite (Exod 22:25; Lev 25:36-37; Deut 23:19-20). Patristic exegesis (Chrysostom, Augustine) struggled with the apparent endorsement of interest-bearing finance. Modern parable-scholarship reads this as parable-internal logic — the parable's master operates by the commercial conventions of the period, not as a theological-ethical statement on interest. Davies-Allison ICC 3.410.

verses.text: ἄρατε οὖν ἀπ' αὐτοῦ τὸ τάλαντον καὶ δότε τῷ ἔχοντι τὰ δέκα τάλαντα·
verses.translit: arate oun ap' autou to talanton kai dote tō echonti ta deka talanta·
verses.notes: The redistribution-judgment — the talent is transferred to the 10-talent servant (the 5+5 servant), not the 4-talent (the 2+2) servant. Suggests the parable's logic of cumulative-faithfulness.

verses.text: τῷ γὰρ ἔχοντι παντὶ δοθήσεται καὶ περισσευθήσεται· τοῦ δὲ μὴ ἔχοντος καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ' αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: tō gar echonti panti dothēsetai kai perisseuthēsetai· tou de mē echontos kai ho echei arthēsetai ap' autou.
verses.notes: **THE 'MATTHEW EFFECT' VERSE** — the aphorism named after this Matthean verse by sociologist Robert K. Merton (1968). **CROSS-CORPUS to Mt 13:12** (verbatim within the Sower-discourse). Synoptic parallels: Mk 4:25; Luke 8:18; 19:26. The cumulative-advantage / cumulative-disadvantage aphorism — appears to be a free-floating wisdom-logion repurposed at multiple discourse-locations.

verses.text: καὶ τὸν ἀχρεῖον δοῦλον ἐκβάλετε εἰς τὸ σκότος τὸ ἐξώτερον· ἐκεῖ ἔσται ὁ κλαυθμὸς καὶ ὁ βρυγμὸς τῶν ὀδόντων.
verses.translit: kai ton achreion doulon ekbalete eis to skotos to exōteron· ekei estai ho klauthmos kai ho brygmos tōn odontōn.
verses.notes: **THE OUTER-DARKNESS / WEEPING-AND-GNASHING-OF-TEETH FORMULA**. Matthean signature judgment-formula — occurs at 8:12; 13:42, 50; 22:13; 24:51; 25:30 (six times). *to skotos to exōteron* (the outer darkness) is Matthew-only. *klauthmos kai brygmos tōn odontōn* — weeping and grinding-of-teeth (rage / despair). The formula's recurrent placement at parable-closures marks the eschatological-judgment moment. *achreion* (useless / worthless) — sharper-edged than v.26 *oknēre*. Davies-Allison ICC 3.410-411.

verses.text: Ὅταν δὲ ἔλθῃ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ δόξῃ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάντες οἱ ἄγγελοι μετ' αὐτοῦ, τότε καθίσει ἐπὶ θρόνου δόξης αὐτοῦ·
verses.translit: Hotan de elthē ho huios tou anthrōpou en tē doxē autou kai pantes hoi angeloi met' autou, tote kathisei epi thronou doxēs autou·
verses.notes: **SHEEP AND GOATS / FINAL JUDGMENT — OPENING (vv.31-46). HIGHEST LENS-RISK PERICOPE OF THE CHAPTER.** Matthean SonderGut (no synoptic parallel). **MAJOR CROSS-CORPUS PARALLELS**: (i) Dan 7:13-14 LXX (the Son-of-Man enthronement); (ii) Dan 7:9-10 (the thrones set up and the books opened); (iii) Zech 14:5 (*pantes hoi hagioi met' autou* — the holy ones with the LORD); (iv) Joel 3:1-12 [4:1-12 MT] (the gathering of nations for judgment in the valley of Jehoshaphat); (v) 1 Enoch 62-63 (the Son of Man on the throne of glory judging the nations — the most direct parallel; the 1 Enoch Parables / Similitudes are the closest extra-canonical analog). *pantes hoi angeloi* — the angelic retinue (variant: some witnesses read *hoi hagioi angeloi* — the holy angels; SBLGNT/NA28 omit *hagioi*). **RAËLIAN CANON CITATION SITE**: the canon reads this scene as 'the Elohim's final return' — the Son of Man with the angelic retinue interpreted as the Elohim civilization returning in their craft. **LENS-RISK FLAG for the Editor**: do NOT pre-resolve toward (a) the Raëlian Elohim-return reading, (b) the orthodox-Christian final-judgment dogma, or (c) the apocalyptic-prophetic / 1 Enoch–style throne-vision tradition. Preserve the Danielic + 1 Enochic intertextual matrix. Davies-Allison ICC 3.418-433; Luz Hermeneia 3.272-296.

verses.text: καὶ συναχθήσονται ἔμπροσθεν αὐτοῦ πάντα τὰ ἔθνη, καὶ ἀφορίσει αὐτοὺς ἀπ' ἀλλήλων, ὥσπερ ὁ ποιμὴν ἀφορίζει τὰ πρόβατα ἀπὸ τῶν ἐρίφων,
verses.translit: kai synachthēsontai emprosthen autou panta ta ethnē, kai aphorisei autous ap' allēlōn, hōsper ho poimēn aphorizei ta probata apo tōn eriphōn,
verses.notes: **MAJOR INTERPRETIVE CRUX — *panta ta ethnē* ('all the nations')**. Three principal interpretive options: (a) all humanity (universalist reading); (b) all non-Christian / gentile nations judged by their treatment of Christians (the 'particularist' or 'ecclesial' reading — Gray 1989); (c) all gentile nations (excluding Israel) judged on their treatment of Israel. Each reading has substantial defenders; the choice is consequential for the 'least of these' interpretation at v.40. Matthew's broader usage of *ethnē* is ambiguous (sometimes 'gentiles,' sometimes 'all peoples including Israel'; cf. 28:19 *panta ta ethnē* in the Great Commission). *aphorisei* (will separate) — the technical legal-judicial term. The shepherd-separating-sheep-from-goats simile: standard ANE pastoral practice (sheep and goats grazed together by day, separated at night for shelter and milking). Davies-Allison ICC 3.421-423.

verses.text: καὶ στήσει τὰ μὲν πρόβατα ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ τὰ δὲ ἐρίφια ἐξ εὐωνύμων.
verses.translit: kai stēsei ta men probata ek dexiōn autou ta de eriphia ex euōnymōn.
verses.notes: Right-hand favored / left-hand disfavored — standard ANE judicial-positional symbolism. *eriphia* (kids / young goats — diminutive); the standard reading reverses to *eriphoi* (goats) at the next verse-level; the diminutive vs simple-form distinction is not interpretively-significant. Note: in Matthew's region (1st-c. Palestine) sheep and goats look superficially similar from a distance and were typically herded together — the parable's image is therefore prosaic, not exotic.

verses.text: τότε ἐρεῖ ὁ βασιλεὺς τοῖς ἐκ δεξιῶν αὐτοῦ· Δεῦτε, οἱ εὐλογημένοι τοῦ πατρός μου, κληρονομήσατε τὴν ἡτοιμασμένην ὑμῖν βασιλείαν ἀπὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
verses.translit: tote erei ho basileus tois ek dexiōn autou· Deute, hoi eulogēmenoi tou patros mou, klēronomēsate tēn hētoimasmenēn hymin basileian apo katabolēs kosmou.
verses.notes: **THE BLESSING-INVITATION**. *ho basileus* — the title 'king' enters here; the Son of Man (v.31) is identified as the eschatological king (Dan 7:14 royal-investiture). *klēronomēsate tēn … basileian* (inherit the kingdom) — inheritance-language (cf. Mt 5:5 *klēronomēsousin tēn gēn*). *apo katabolēs kosmou* (from the foundation of the world) — pre-temporal preparation; cf. Eph 1:4; 1 Pet 1:20; Rev 13:8; 17:8. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: the pre-cosmic preparation echo is engaged in some lens-readings as 'engineered-from-the-Elohim-arrival' — preserve text, document for Editor.

verses.text: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ἐδίψησα καὶ ἐποτίσατέ με, ξένος ἤμην καὶ συνηγάγετέ με,
verses.translit: epeinasa gar kai edōkate moi phagein, edipsēsa kai epotisate me, xenos ēmēn kai synēgagete me,
verses.notes: **THE SIX-FOLD MERCY-LIST — FIRST HALF (vv.35-36)**. Six categories of distress + responsive action: (1) hungry / fed; (2) thirsty / given drink; (3) stranger / welcomed; (4) naked / clothed; (5) sick / visited; (6) prisoner / visited. The list compresses standard 1st-c. Jewish-charity traditions (cf. Isa 58:6-7; Job 22:6-7; 31:16-22; Ezek 18:7-9; T. Jos. 1:5-7; Sir 7:32-35) but distinctively elevates *xenos* (stranger) and visiting prisoners. *synēgagete* (gathered in / welcomed [as a guest]) — the hospitality term. Davies-Allison ICC 3.423-426.

verses.text: γυμνὸς καὶ περιεβάλετέ με, ἠσθένησα καὶ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με, ἐν φυλακῇ ἤμην καὶ ἤλθατε πρός με.
verses.translit: gymnos kai periebalete me, ēsthenēsa kai epeskepsasthe me, en phylakē ēmēn kai ēlthate pros me.
verses.notes: **THE SIX-FOLD MERCY-LIST — SECOND HALF**. *gymnos* — naked or insufficiently clothed (the latter is the more common 1st-c. usage). *ēsthenēsa* — was sick. *epeskepsasthe* (visited / looked after) — same root as LXX divine *episkopē* (visitation). *en phylakē* — in prison; the visiting-of-prisoners is the most striking item, since identifying with a prisoner risked legal exposure (cf. Heb 13:3; 2 Tim 1:16-17).

verses.text: τότε ἀποκριθήσονται αὐτῷ οἱ δίκαιοι λέγοντες· Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα καὶ ἐθρέψαμεν, ἢ διψῶντα καὶ ἐποτίσαμεν;
verses.translit: tote apokrithēsontai autō hoi dikaioi legontes· Kyrie, pote se eidomen peinōnta kai ethrepsamen, ē dipsōnta kai epotisamen;
verses.notes: **THE RIGHTEOUS'S SURPRISE-QUESTION**. *hoi dikaioi* — the righteous; technical Matthean term (cf. 13:43, 49; 25:46). The surprise structure — the righteous did not know they were ministering to the king — is parable-internal evidence against any 'works-righteousness' reading: the meritorious are characterized precisely by NOT having kept score. Davies-Allison ICC 3.426-427.

verses.text: πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ξένον καὶ συνηγάγομεν, ἢ γυμνὸν καὶ περιεβάλομεν;
verses.translit: pote de se eidomen xenon kai synēgagomen, ē gymnon kai periebalomen;
verses.notes: Continuation of the surprise-question, items 3-4 of the six-fold list.

verses.text: πότε δέ σε εἴδομεν ἀσθενοῦντα ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ ἤλθομεν πρός σε;
verses.translit: pote de se eidomen asthenounta ē en phylakē kai ēlthomen pros se;
verses.notes: Items 5-6 of the six-fold list. The repeated *pote* (when) structures the litany.

verses.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ βασιλεὺς ἐρεῖ αὐτοῖς· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφ' ὅσον ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἀδελφῶν μου τῶν ἐλαχίστων, ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.
verses.translit: kai apokritheis ho basileus erei autois· Amēn legō hymin, eph' hoson epoiēsate heni toutōn tōn adelphōn mou tōn elachistōn, emoi epoiēsate.
verses.notes: **THE CENTRAL EXEGETICAL CRUX OF THE PERICOPE — 'TO WHOM' IS THE LOCUS CLASSICUS**. *heni toutōn tōn adelphōn mou tōn elachistōn* — 'to one of the least of these brothers of mine.' The interpretive history is vast (Gray 1989 *The Least of My Brothers* is a 350-page history-of-interpretation monograph on this verse alone). Three principal readings: **(A) UNIVERSAL READING** — 'the least' = all suffering humanity; ethical-universalism reading (patristic and Reformation mainstream; modern liberal-humanitarian); 'brothers' as inclusive familial term. **(B) ECCLESIAL / PARTICULARIST READING** — 'the least of my brothers' = Christians / disciples in distress; the nations are judged by their treatment of the Jesus-followers (Bornkamm, Jeremias, France NICNT 956-958; Wilkins 1995). The Matthean usage of *adelphoi mou* elsewhere is exclusively for disciples (12:48-50; 28:10), and the missionary-mandate Mt 10:40-42 explicitly identifies these 'little ones' with the apostles. **(C) JEWISH-PARTICULAR READING** — 'brothers' = ethnic Jewish people; the gentiles judged on treatment of Israel. The Matthean text is irreducibly ambiguous, and the choice between (A), (B), and (C) is consequential for the entire pericope's meaning. **MAJOR LENS-RISK FLAG**: the Raëlian canon engages this verse — preserve all three readings; do NOT pre-resolve. *eph' hoson epoiēsate … emoi epoiēsate* — the identification-of-the-king-with-the-suffering is the unifying claim regardless of which (A)/(B)/(C) reading is taken. Davies-Allison ICC 3.428-429; Snodgrass 2008 555-559.

verses.text: Τότε ἐρεῖ καὶ τοῖς ἐξ εὐωνύμων· Πορεύεσθε ἀπ' ἐμοῦ κατηραμένοι εἰς τὸ πῦρ τὸ αἰώνιον τὸ ἡτοιμασμένον τῷ διαβόλῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀγγέλοις αὐτοῦ.
verses.translit: Tote erei kai tois ex euōnymōn· Poreuesthe ap' emou katēramenoi eis to pyr to aiōnion to hētoimasmenon tō diabolō kai tois angelois autou.
verses.notes: **THE CURSE-DISMISSAL**. *katēramenoi* (cursed ones) — note the lack of agency-specification (passive participle without explicit divine agent; not *katēramenoi hypo tou patros mou* parallel to the v.34 *hoi eulogēmenoi tou patros mou*) — the curse is announced without claimed origin in the Father, suggesting self-incurred consequence. *to pyr to aiōnion* (the eternal fire) — *aiōnion* is theologically loaded: 'eternal' (orthodox/Augustinian) vs 'of-the-age' (some patristic universalists; Origen) vs 'lasting / age-long.' *to hētoimasmenon tō diabolō kai tois angelois autou* — prepared for the devil and his angels (NOT primarily for humans; the destination is fundamentally diabological, humans share it as the result of unmerciful choice). **CROSS-CORPUS to 1 Enoch 10:13; 18:11-16; 21:7-10** (the fiery abyss prepared for the rebellious angels); 2 Pet 2:4; Jude 6 (Tartarus / chains-of-darkness for the angels). The 1 Enoch tradition of the punishment-locus prepared for the fallen Watchers is the primary intertextual frame. **P45 CROSS-COLLATION**: P45 preserves this verse; reading agrees with Vaticanus + Sinaiticus. **LENS-RISK FLAG**: do NOT pre-resolve the *aiōnion* duration-question; document the lexical-debate.

verses.text: ἐπείνασα γὰρ καὶ οὐκ ἐδώκατέ μοι φαγεῖν, ἐδίψησα καὶ οὐκ ἐποτίσατέ με,
verses.translit: epeinasa gar kai ouk edōkate moi phagein, edipsēsa kai ouk epotisate me,
verses.notes: Inverse of v.35. The structural symmetry: each affirmative item of the righteous's mercy-list is negated. Note: the indictment is not for active harm but for omission of mercy — the sin-of-omission frame. Davies-Allison ICC 3.430.

verses.text: ξένος ἤμην καὶ οὐ συνηγάγετέ με, γυμνὸς καὶ οὐ περιεβάλετέ με, ἀσθενὴς καὶ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐκ ἐπεσκέψασθέ με.
verses.translit: xenos ēmēn kai ou synēgagete me, gymnos kai ou periebalete me, asthenēs kai en phylakē kai ouk epeskepsasthe me.
verses.notes: Continuation of the inverse-mercy-list. Items 3-6 negated. Note the slight compression vs vv.35-36 (asthenēs + en phylakē are merged into a single clause).

verses.text: τότε ἀποκριθήσονται καὶ αὐτοὶ λέγοντες· Κύριε, πότε σε εἴδομεν πεινῶντα ἢ διψῶντα ἢ ξένον ἢ γυμνὸν ἢ ἀσθενῆ ἢ ἐν φυλακῇ καὶ οὐ διηκονήσαμέν σοι;
verses.translit: tote apokrithēsontai kai autoi legontes· Kyrie, pote se eidomen peinōnta ē dipsōnta ē xenon ē gymnon ē asthenē ē en phylakē kai ou diēkonēsamen soi;
verses.notes: Inverse of vv.37-39. The cursed equally surprised — symmetrically did not know. Note the structural parallel: BOTH groups protest ignorance of the king's identification with the needy. The criterion is purely behavioral; neither group calculated. *diēkonēsamen* (served) — diakonia-language.

verses.text: τότε ἀποκριθήσεται αὐτοῖς λέγων· Ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐφ' ὅσον οὐκ ἐποιήσατε ἑνὶ τούτων τῶν ἐλαχίστων, οὐδὲ ἐμοὶ ἐποιήσατε.
verses.translit: tote apokrithēsetai autois legōn· Amēn legō hymin, eph' hoson ouk epoiēsate heni toutōn tōn elachistōn, oude emoi epoiēsate.
verses.notes: Inverse-form of v.40. Note: this verse OMITS *tōn adelphōn mou* — the curse-formulation reads simply *heni toutōn tōn elachistōn* without the brothers-of-mine specification. This omission is exegetically significant for the (A)/(B)/(C) reading-debate at v.40: if 'brothers of mine' restricts in v.40, why does v.45 not also restrict? Reading-(A) advocates (universal) take v.45 as the controlling formulation; reading-(B) advocates (ecclesial) argue the *adelphōn mou* is implicit. Davies-Allison ICC 3.431. **MAJOR LENS-RISK FLAG**.

verses.text: καὶ ἀπελεύσονται οὗτοι εἰς κόλασιν αἰώνιον, οἱ δὲ δίκαιοι εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
verses.translit: kai apeleusontai houtoi eis kolasin aiōnion, hoi de dikaioi eis zōēn aiōnion.
verses.notes: **THE FINAL TWO-FOLD PRONOUNCEMENT**. *kolasin aiōnion* (eternal punishment) vs *zōēn aiōnion* (eternal life). The parallel construction with the same *aiōnion* qualifier creates a famous lexical-symmetry: if 'eternal life' is unending, then 'eternal punishment' is unending; or alternatively, if *aiōnion* means 'of-the-age' in both, then the symmetry is between two age-bounded destinies. *kolasis* — the noun (Matthew-only NT usage of this noun) means specifically 'punishment' in 1st-c. Greek (in contrast to *timōria* which has retributive overtones; cf. 4 Macc 8:9; Wisd Sol 19:4). The verb-form *kolazō* appears at Acts 4:21; 2 Pet 2:9. The orthodox-eternal vs annihilationist vs universalist-restorationist reading-debate (Athanasius/Augustine vs Edward White et al. vs Origen/Gregory of Nyssa) takes its locus classicus here. **CROSS-CORPUS to Dan 12:2 LXX** (the two-fold eschatological fate — *eis zōēn aiōnion* and *eis oneidismon aiōnion* — the verbal echo is direct). The structural-symmetry plus the Daniel intertext is the philological anchor. Davies-Allison ICC 3.432-433. **MAJOR LENS-RISK FLAG**: preserve the *aiōnion* duration-debate; do NOT pre-resolve.
